description: ODC: STATIC ENTITY WITH RECORDS written op by op (mirrors tests/jobs/static-entity.json). The census counts IStaticEntityRecord in 26 of the 44 real modules and the ODC lane only created it inside the spec op: here it is born through the raw verbs, which is the way when you want an attribute beyond the trio Id/Label/Order. The convention (which the API does not state) is Id Integer WITHOUT AutoNumber (the ODC Studio refuses live 'StaticEntity Auto Number') + IdentifierAttribute and an Id written in each record, Label Text + LabelAttribute, Order Integer + OrderByAttribute - note that the Id of a static entity is Integer, unlike the Long Integer of an IServerEntity. Each record is created with type IRecord and the object that is born is an IStaticEntityRecord; the value of each column is written in $record/<Attribute> prop Value and in ODC what holds it is an IRecordAttributeValue - the SAME type that serves as the value of the sample record of a normal entity (see delete-attribute-no-consumers.json), which is why it counts as derived use and does not block a delete. The second half of the job proves what the records are for: a normal entity with a FK to the static entity and default Entities.WfClaimStage.Received.

ops.value: Etapas de um processo de sinistro, em ordem

ops._why: a static entity has Id Integer; it is the ODC IServerEntity that has Long Integer (contrast in WfClaimFile, further down)

a static entity NEVER has Id AutoNumber: the ODC Studio refuses live with 'The app uses StaticEntity Auto Number, which is not supported on this version' (the headless Verify does not catch it). Each record gets its Id below
without an identifier the entity does not pass the Verify; and it is this attribute that generates the IIdentifierType 'WfClaimStage Identifier' used further down
it is the Label that the platform shows when the record appears in a screen or in a dropdown
defines the order in which the records come out, independent of the Id; the dump further down does NOT come out in this order, because the tree of the model is not the reading order
the attribute BEYOND the trio: it is through it that the static entity stops being just a label and starts holding data per record. It is the reason to write this job op by op instead of a spec line

ops.value: Marca as etapas que fecham o sinistro

ops.name: Received
ops._why: PLATFORM DIFFERENCE: the type of the create is IRecord in both lanes, but the object that comes back in the dump is IRecord in O11 and IStaticEntityRecord in ODC - and the latter is the name that the census counts. It is already born with one IRecordAttributeValue per attribute, empty, waiting for the Value
without AutoNumber the Id of each record is written by the job, like the other values
$record/<Attribute> reaches the value of that column in that record; the Value is an expression, so the text carries the OutSystems quotes inside the JSON quotes
the Label does not have to equal the name of the record: the name is a code identifier (Entities.WfClaimStage.UnderReview), the Label is what the user reads
the only record with IsFinal at True: the value per record is what distinguishes this static entity from a list of labels

ops.name: WfClaimFile
ops._why: the second half: a normal entity that CONSUMES the static entity. Without a consumer, a static entity passes the Verify all the same (it does not get UnusedElement, unlike a structure), but what the 26 real modules do is this

ops.value: Sinistro em curso, com a etapa em que esta

ops._why: the promised contrast: a normal entity has Id Long Integer, a static entity has Integer
the FK is written by the NAME of the identifier type that the static entity generated by itself when it received the IdentifierAttribute

Entities.<Static>.<Record> is the only way to cite a record in an expression, and it is valid in any expression property (default, aggregate filter, If condition). In ODC the expression property is written by ExpressionDefinition.Parse, which is what links this text to the IStaticEntityRecord created above - so the record now has a REAL consumer
reads back the entity: EntityKind Static, Records 3, Attributes 4 and Identifier/Label/OrderBy pointing to the attributes created here
proves the value per record: the object is an IRecordAttributeValue with Attribute = IsFinal and Value = True
proves the default: the text comes back as Entities.WfClaimStage.Received, already relinked to the record

proves the whole tree: 4 IEntityAttribute, 3 IStaticEntityRecord with one IRecordAttributeValue per attribute (the one of the Id with the value written by the job), each value held in an ITextBasedExpression (in O11 the same place appears as IExpression), and also the GetWfClaimStage and the 'WfClaimStage Identifier' that the platform generates by itself. The records do NOT come out in creation order: what rules the reading order is the OrderByAttribute, not the tree
proves that the record Received is consumed by the default of WfClaimFile.StageId: a static entity record is a model object like any other, with consumers and with delete refusal
